title: A better heat conductor
hook: Change thermal conductivity and predict conducted heat rate.
misconception: conducted heat rate stays fixed when thermal conductivity doubles.
objective: Apply Q̇ = kAΔT/L to compare conducted heat rate when thermal conductivity changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With steady one-dimensional conduction with fixed area thickness and temperature difference, Q̇ = kAΔT/L. When thermal conductivity doubles, conducted heat rate becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q̇ = kAΔT/L; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider steady one-dimensional conduction with fixed area thickness and temperature difference, with a nonzero initial result. If thermal conductivity triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on conducted heat rate?
recall.why: Apply Q̇ = kAΔT/L under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
